source: Reconciled against the Data Dawgs site, Worker source and inspected upstream projects on 2026-08-08. College Football roadmap ideas added from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.
note: Two kinds of entry share this inventory. kind "tool" (NFL) carries delivery status. kind "roadmap-idea" (College Football) carries recommendation plus evidence-backed lifecycle and implementation state. A CFB artifact may be implemented without any MCP tool; candidate_mcp_tools are reservations and remain non-callable unless the independent Worker registry proves otherwise.

cfb_roadmap.note: The 12-step ordering is directional, not an irreversible commitment; dependencies ultimately determine the actual build sequence. Recommendations are recommendations, not permanent truths.

recommendation_classes.build: Strong recommendation: fits the DATA → MODELS/DETERMINISTIC TOOLS → API/MCP → AI → HUMAN DECISION architecture with a plausible path to useful production functionality. Modifiers distinguish foundation, high-priority and decision-engine work.
recommendation_classes.lab: Promising hypothesis worth testing. It must demonstrate incremental predictive or decision value before promotion, and it is explicitly allowed to fail.
recommendation_classes.defer: Interesting, but expected signal, data quality or maintenance economics do not justify building it now. The idea is kept.
recommendation_classes.avoid-initially: Possible eventual value, but current dependency, scraping, legal, reliability, maintenance or architectural concerns make it undesirable right now.
recommendation_classes.not-needed: Redundant with the architecture Data Dawgs is already building.

lifecycle.policy: Ideas are never silently deleted. Moving to the Graveyard means "tested or evaluated, and currently not worth active resources" — the record, its history and its lessons are retained so the Graveyard works as institutional memory, not a trash can.
lifecycle.revival_question: What would have to become true for us to dig this Dawg back up?

governance.name: Source Provenance
governance.principle: Every important derived CFB artifact should eventually be traceable to its source datasets and processing versions, the way the NFL backbone pins commits and snapshot hashes.

governance.name: Snapshotting / Receipts
governance.principle: Forecasts and model outputs used for grading must be frozen before outcomes occur. This is the same receipts discipline already live for NFL models.
governance.applies_to: every CFB forecast or model output

governance.name: Model Cards
governance.principle: Important models eventually document purpose, target, features, training window, validation design, known limitations, calibration, performance, failure modes, version and retirement status.
governance.applies_to: every CFB model promoted past the lab

governance.name: Baseline Requirement
governance.principle: No sophisticated model is promoted merely because it is sophisticated. Everything is benchmarked against the market and simple interpretable baselines.

governance.name: Incremental Information Test
governance.principle: New models and features must demonstrate value relative to what Data Dawgs already knows before they earn production resources.
governance.applies_to: every CFB model and feature family

governance.name: Correlation Awareness
governance.principle: Multiple correlated models are not multiple independent pieces of evidence. Consensus construction must measure error correlation before treating agreement as confirmation.

governance.name: Uncertainty
governance.principle: Avoid false precision, especially for weak or incomplete datasets such as NIL information. Outputs carry uncertainty and their date.

source_headings: CFBD Model Training Pack / educational modeling resources

data.name: Model Scoreboard / Mean & Conflict
data.intended_user_value: Compare dated nfelo and 538 Classic beliefs game by game.
data.required_data: Uses the normalized prospective nfelo and 538 Classic receipts published by Data Dawgs.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Interactive game table with metric/source states.
data.ai_language_requirement: Explain the equal-weight mean, range, dissent and missing models without claiming a validated consensus blend.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_model_scoreboard read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Transparent Disagreement Engine
data.intended_user_value: Show mean, median, range, standard deviation and decision-boundary splits.
data.required_data: Any list of probabilities, plus the current scoreboard.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Belief-summary lab and per-game descriptive statistics.
data.ai_language_requirement: Descriptive uncertainty only; never call disagreement a predictive edge.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_summarize_beliefs read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: 538 Classic Elo
data.intended_user_value: Provide a permanent simple benchmark/control.
data.required_data: Pinned official reference, completed canonical game history and the 2026 schedule snapshot.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Prospective scoreboard column plus one-game probability calculator.
data.ai_language_requirement: Permanent simple benchmark; reproduced historically and still ungraded prospectively.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_elo_game read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: nfelo Power Ratings
data.intended_user_value: Use a dated public model output with Data Dawgs validation.
data.required_data: 2026-08-06 nfelo snapshot and existing historical backtest.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Existing nfelo page plus Pound scoreboard.
data.ai_language_requirement: State that the backtest overlaps optimization and has not established out-of-sample skill.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_analyze_matchup read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: nfeloml EP / EPA / WP
data.intended_user_value: Offer deterministic play-level inference primitives.
data.required_data: MIT package and canonical play inputs.
data.ai_language_requirement: Do not present upstream calibration as Data Dawgs-verified.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: Static GitHub Pages cannot run the Python/XGBoost package; a precompute job or Worker-compatible port is required.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Run the MIT package in a scheduled precompute job with schema checks and publish static output, or build and validate a Worker-compatible inference port.

data.name: QB Context
data.intended_user_value: Measure starter/replacement and passing-context deltas.
data.required_data: Lawful dated output plus starter mapping.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Inventory card; no invented QB adjustment.
data.ai_language_requirement: Context is optional and unvalidated for DFS or game forecasting.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: No verified reusable license and no canonical Data Dawgs adapter.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Obtain a reusable license, permission, or lawful dated output; then build the starter mapping, adapter, and prospective validation.

data.name: Weighted EPA
data.intended_user_value: Compare context-weighted EPA with ordinary EPA.
data.required_data: Lawful methodology or output plus canonical play data.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Inventory card and explicit ordinary-EPA baseline.
data.ai_language_requirement: Any improvement claim waits on fixed out-of-sample tests.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: No verified reusable license and no Data Dawgs implementation.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Obtain a reusable methodology or licensed output, implement the weighting against canonical play data, and test it against ordinary EPA out of sample.

data.name: SRS / Win-Total Ratings
data.intended_user_value: Estimate team strength, priors and schedule difficulty.
data.required_data: Timestamped lawful win-total market inputs and schedule.
data.ai_language_requirement: Market inputs must carry source, time and vig handling.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: No verified reusable license or licensed market feed.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Secure a lawful win-total feed and reusable methodology, then publish versioned preseason and weekly ratings from canonical schedules.

data.name: Home-Field Adjustment Tracker
data.intended_user_value: Inspect the effect of a transparent HFA assumption.
data.required_data: User-supplied ratings and HFA; site defaults are dated.
data.ai_language_requirement: Labels inputs modelled and does not claim the default is current truth.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_elo_game read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.exact_blocker: Historical HFA tracking feed is not built.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Build a canonical historical-game input, estimate HFA by declared period/context, and publish a dated series with uncertainty.

data.name: Unit Ratings
data.intended_user_value: Separate pass, rush and special-teams strengths.
data.required_data: Lawful unit outputs and canonical play data.
data.ai_language_requirement: Upstream performance numbers remain upstream claims.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: Research/educational language is not a reusable software license.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Obtain a reusable license, permission, or lawful output; normalize unit ratings to canonical teams and replicate performance claims independently.

data.name: Probability / Spread Translation
data.intended_user_value: Translate win probability into expected margin and cover estimates.
data.required_data: User probability and dated Data Dawgs normal residual SD.
data.ai_language_requirement: Calls the result MODELLED and names the normal, independent, no-key-number assumption.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_translate_probability read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Market Normalizer
data.intended_user_value: Normalize American odds, implied probability, hold and devig probabilities.
data.required_data: User-entered prices.
data.ai_language_requirement: No sportsbook feed, closing-line claim or vendor attribution.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_devig_market read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Cover Probability / EV
data.intended_user_value: Turn a declared probability and price into break-even and expected value.
data.required_data: User probability and price, or the modelled normal translator.
data.ai_language_requirement: Distinguishes the user/model probability from the price-implied probability.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_calculate_bet_ev read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Odds Converter
data.intended_user_value: Convert American odds to decimal odds and implied probability.
data.required_data: User-entered odds.
data.ai_language_requirement: Deterministic conversion; no predictive claim.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_convert_odds read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Parlay Calculator
data.intended_user_value: Compound declared leg prices.
data.required_data: User-entered American odds.
data.ai_language_requirement: Multiplies declared prices; does not claim a correlation-aware joint probability.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_price_parlay read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Hedge Calculator
data.intended_user_value: Size the opposite side for equal net outcome.
data.required_data: Original stake/price and hedge price.
data.ai_language_requirement: Arithmetic, not advice; ignores limits, tax and execution risk.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_calculate_hedge read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: NFL Passer Rating
data.intended_user_value: Reproduce the public deterministic NFL passer-rating formula.
data.required_data: Attempts, completions, yards, touchdowns and interceptions.
data.ai_language_requirement: Descriptive statistic, not a forecast or QBR substitute.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_nfl_passer_rating read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Forecast Grader
data.intended_user_value: Compute Brier score and log loss for one declared forecast.
data.required_data: Probability and binary outcome.
data.ai_language_requirement: One observation is not model validation; sample size stays visible.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Keep dd_score_forecast read-only and align its contract with the public JSON.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Immutable Multi-Model Receipts
data.intended_user_value: Make prospective forecasts auditable after outcomes are known.
data.required_data: Normalized forecasts, input snapshots and market state before kickoff.
data.human_facing_ui_requirement: Contract and link to the existing 2026 receipt ledger.
data.ai_language_requirement: Never mix backtests and prospective forecasts.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: Regime Analysis
data.intended_user_value: Evaluate performance by declared football conditions.
data.required_data: Adequate prospective comparable samples and predeclared slices.
data.ai_language_requirement: Post-hoc slices are exploratory; sample sizes and multiple-comparison risk must be shown.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Add a read-only Worker tool only after the required deterministic data or runtime is validated.
data.exact_blocker: Two-model prospective receipts exist, but no 2026 outcomes have occurred or been graded yet.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Accumulate adequate prospective samples, preregister slices and minimum counts, and mark post-hoc analysis exploratory.

data.name: Ensemble Lab
data.intended_user_value: Compare mean, median and later weighted blends.
data.required_data: User-entered probabilities or future normalized forecasts.
data.ai_language_requirement: Complex methods wait until they beat equal weight on held-out data.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Expose the staged deterministic browser function through a read-only Worker tool using the published calculator contract.
data.exact_blocker: Weighted ensembles need prospective error history.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: Accumulate prospective model errors, then benchmark mean, median and candidate weighting methods against the market and best individual model.

data.name: NFL Data Backbone
data.intended_user_value: Create validated, reproducible canonical snapshots for every model.
data.required_data: nfelodcm, GitHub Actions, schema/freshness gates and snapshot retention.
data.ai_language_requirement: Fail closed on schema drift and suspicious row-count changes.
data.mcp_api_requirement: Static public schedule; no MCP calculation is required.
data.minimum_path_to_completion: No known blocker for the deployed scope.

data.name: SportsDataverse Bulk-Data Ingestion
data.rationale: SportsDataverse already publishes analysis-ready CFB data. Reproducing the ESPN ingestion and enrichment ecosystem would be undifferentiated maintenance work.
data.expected_value: Primary bulk-data substrate: SportsDataverse → Data Dawgs canonical CFB layer feeding every downstream dataset.
data.data_source_requirements: Pinned SportsDataverse CFB releases with schema, freshness and row-count gates at ingest, mirroring the NFL backbone.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — this is infrastructure every deterministic CFB tool sits on.
data.validation_requirement: Ingest gates fail closed on schema drift or suspicious row counts; retained snapshots make every load reproducible.
data.risks_limitations: Upstream schema drift and inherited coverage gaps; the layer must never silently pass upstream errors downstream.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: CFBD Enrichment / Model Ingestion
data.rationale: CollegeFootballData.com is an enrichment and model feed — SP+, FPI, SRS, recruiting, talent, returning production, schedules — not the sole center of the architecture.
data.expected_value: CFBD → Data Dawgs canonical CFB layer: ratings and talent enrichments the bulk substrate does not carry.
data.data_source_requirements: CFBD API access with keys held outside the public repo; dated pulls; per-feed schema checks.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — feeds the ratings registry and talent datasets.
data.validation_requirement: Every pull dated and snapshotted; feed-level gates; upstream numbers stay labelled as upstream claims until independently validated.
data.risks_limitations: API dependency, rate limits and upstream revisions; enrichment fields can change definitions between seasons.

Published 934 validated games with unique IDs and a reproducible snapshot hash.

data.name: Canonical CFB Games
data.rationale: A canonical cfb_games dataset is the spine every schedule, rating, receipt and simulator joins against.
data.expected_value: Durable game IDs, results and kickoff context for all downstream CFB work.
data.data_source_requirements: SportsDataverse schedules/results reconciled with CFBD reference data.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — reference layer.
data.validation_requirement: Unique game IDs, season/week coverage gates and snapshot hashes, like /data/nfl-schedule.json.
data.risks_limitations: FBS/FCS boundary cases, cancellations and rescheduling need explicit rules.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Canonical CFB Play-by-Play
data.rationale: A canonical cfb_plays layer carries the useful play-level fields Data Dawgs needs without forcing downstream applications to understand the entire upstream schema.
data.expected_value: The substrate for EPA, success rate, fourth-down modelling, CPOE, xREPA and unit ratings.
data.data_source_requirements: SportsDataverse play-by-play with EPA/WP fields; documented field selection and derivation notes.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — every play-level deterministic tool reads it.
data.validation_requirement: Row-count and coverage gates per season; spot-checks against published aggregates before anything downstream ships.
data.risks_limitations: CFB play-by-play is messier than NFL data: garbage-time definitions, clock quirks and missing fields need explicit handling.

data.name: Canonical CFB Team-Game Dataset
data.rationale: Canonical cfb_team_game: one row per team per game, aggregated once, consistently, instead of separately inside every tool.
data.expected_value: Shared team-game aggregates for ratings, the fraud detector and the team-week layer.
data.data_source_requirements: Derived from canonical plays and games.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — aggregate layer.
data.validation_requirement: Aggregates reconcile with the play layer; derivations documented and reproducible.
data.risks_limitations: Aggregation choices (garbage time, overtime) must be declared, not implicit.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Canonical CFB Player-Game Dataset
data.rationale: Canonical cfb_player_game gives player-level analysis one consistent home instead of ad-hoc extraction per question.
data.expected_value: Player-game rows for CPOE, xREPA, QBR comparisons and portal/talent follow-up analysis.
data.data_source_requirements: Derived from canonical plays plus roster identity resolution.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — aggregate layer.
data.validation_requirement: Player IDs resolve through the roster layer; totals reconcile with team-game rows.
data.risks_limitations: Player attribution in CFB play-by-play is incomplete for some seasons and stat types.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: CFB Rosters / Identity Resolution
data.rationale: Canonical cfb_rosters with durable IDs and cross-source identity handling. Portal, recruiting and player analysis all die without it.
data.expected_value: Durable player identity across SportsDataverse, CFBD, recruiting classes and portal moves.
data.data_source_requirements: SportsDataverse and CFBD rosters; documented matching rules; manual override table for hard cases.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — identity layer.
data.validation_requirement: Match-rate reporting per source pair; ambiguous matches flagged rather than silently merged.
data.risks_limitations: Name collisions, transfers and roster churn make identity the highest-touch dataset in the foundation.

data.name: CFB Market Dataset
data.rationale: Canonical spreads, totals and relevant market observations. The market is the permanent benchmark every model must beat.
data.expected_value: Market baselines for grading; closing lines retained wherever possible for model evaluation.
data.data_source_requirements: A lawful, dated market feed with book and timestamp provenance — the same gate the NFL side already enforces.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — benchmark layer.
data.validation_requirement: Every observation carries book, timestamp and line; closing-line retention is checked, not assumed.
data.risks_limitations: Historical closing lines with provenance are the hardest part; unprovenanced market numbers stay out, as on the NFL side.

data.name: CFB Ratings Registry
data.rationale: Canonical cfb_ratings stores independent rating and forecast systems consistently — SP+, FPI, SRS, Elo, Data Dawgs EPA ratings, the betting market and eventual Data Dawgs predictive models.
data.expected_value: Normalized expected margin, win probability, predicted total where applicable, and team strength — the comparable outputs everything downstream reads.
data.data_source_requirements: CFBD ratings feeds, the canonical market dataset and internally computed ratings, all dated per system per week.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — registry reads are deterministic lookups.
data.validation_requirement: Each system documents its normalization into comparable outputs; unconverted or unavailable fields stay null rather than being invented.
data.risks_limitations: Normalizing heterogeneous systems into comparable outputs is where silent errors live; the NFL model-contracts approach applies.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: CFB Talent Dataset
data.rationale: Canonical talent, recruiting, returning-production and portal features in one dated dataset instead of scattered pulls.
data.expected_value: The feature substrate for the talent/portal ideas and preseason priors.
data.data_source_requirements: CFBD recruiting, talent, returning production and portal feeds keyed to canonical rosters.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect — feature layer.
data.validation_requirement: Feature families dated and versioned; coverage per team per season reported.
data.risks_limitations: Portal data is noisier than recruiting composites; coverage varies by season.

data.name: CFB Team-Week Analytical Layer
data.rationale: The canonical cfb_team_week layer is the standardized analytical substrate for downstream CFB tools.
data.expected_value: One dated row per team per week carrying the candidate metric set: EPA/play, offensive/defensive EPA, dropback and rush EPA, success rate, explosive rate, havoc, early-down EPA, late-down success, garbage-time-filtered metrics, rolling 3- and 5-game metrics, home/away splits, opponent-adjusted versions, strength of schedule, market performance and closing-line error.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays, team-game aggregates and the market dataset.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — team profiles and comparisons become deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Metric definitions documented once and spot-checked against published sources; opponent adjustment validated against known cases before anything downstream trusts it.
data.risks_limitations: Opponent adjustment and garbage-time filters are modelling choices, and must be labelled as such rather than presented as observation.

data.name: Compact Public CFB Outputs
data.rationale: Publish compact derived outputs rather than dumping massive play-by-play datasets into the website repository — the same envelope-and-manifest discipline as the existing /data/ contract.
data.expected_value: A possible /data/cfb/ family: manifest.json, teams.json, games-latest.json, team-week-latest.json, ratings-latest.json, disagreement-latest.json, model-grades.json.
data.data_source_requirements: The canonical CFB layers above; every file carries as_of, source and a manifest entry.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — static surfaces are the cheapest deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Same validator contract as existing /data/: envelope fields mandatory, manifest agreement enforced.
data.risks_limitations: Derived outputs drift from their sources unless rebuild discipline is enforced, exactly as AGENTS.md warns for the NFL data.

data.name: Full Offline-Reprocessable Raw Pipeline
data.rationale: A raw → enriched → canonical archival pipeline with manifests and hashes is worth preserving as an option, but duplicating SportsDataverse infrastructure merely because we can is exactly the wrong instinct.
data.expected_value: Full reprocessability if upstream sources become unreliable or if a question needs fields the canonical layer dropped.
data.data_source_requirements: Bulk raw archives with storage and versioning costs accepted up front.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Indirect.
data.validation_requirement: A concrete case where the canonical layer was insufficient — before any build starts.
data.risks_limitations: High storage and maintenance cost for value that SportsDataverse already provides.

data.name: Static SQLite / Browser-Queryable Explorer
data.rationale: An OpenCFB-style static SQLite interface would let large datasets be queried without API credentials. Test the actual use case before committing.
data.expected_value: Ad-hoc exploration beyond what compact JSON surfaces answer.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical CFB layers packed into a versioned static database.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — client-side SQL over a dated snapshot.
data.validation_requirement: Demonstrated real queries that the compact outputs cannot serve.
data.risks_limitations: Large static payloads against unknown demand; stats.html already shows the weight of heavy in-browser data.

data.name: CFB Model Disagreement Lab
data.rationale: Compare independent models — SP+, FPI, SRS, Elo, DD EPA, DD predictive model, market — for individual games and teams. The purpose is not showing rankings; it is surfacing meaningful disagreement.
data.expected_value: The CFB counterpart of the live NFL scoreboard: where credible systems disagree is where attention belongs.
data.data_source_requirements: The ratings registry with normalized comparable outputs.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — descriptive disagreement statistics are deterministic.
data.validation_requirement: Descriptive only until graded: disagreement is not a predictive edge, matching the NFL Pound language.
data.risks_limitations: Correlated systems can agree and still be wrong; the display must not read agreement as confirmation.

data.notes: Consolidates the receipts idea with the Snapshotting / Receipts governance principle: the principle (cfb-gov-snapshotting) states the rule; this entry is the build that implements it for CFB.
data.name: CFB Model Receipts / Historical Grading
data.rationale: Grade model forecasts historically, with forecast snapshots preserved before outcomes so evaluation is genuinely out-of-sample. Extends the snapshotting/receipts discipline already live for NFL models to CFB.
data.expected_value: Spread MAE and RMSE, moneyline Brier score, calibration, ATS versus closing line, total error, performance by season and week, and performance conditional on large disagreement or on market-versus-efficiency splits.
data.data_source_requirements: The ratings registry, the market dataset with closing lines, and append-only frozen forecast snapshots.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — grading a frozen ledger is deterministic.
data.validation_requirement: Receipts frozen before kickoff, never mixed with backtests — the exact rule the NFL ledger enforces.
data.risks_limitations: Grading against closing lines depends on the market dataset clearing its provenance gate.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.notes: Consolidates the consensus-engine idea with the Correlation Awareness governance principle: cfb-gov-correlation states the rule; this entry is the capability that operationalizes it.
data.name: CFB Model Diversity / Consensus Engine
data.rationale: Measure correlations among model errors; never treat agreement between highly correlated models as independent evidence. A diversity-adjusted consensus is built only from demonstrated incremental information.
data.expected_value: A consensus that knows how many independent opinions it actually contains — strongly aligned with model-risk management.
data.data_source_requirements: Graded receipts across enough games to estimate error correlations.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — a declared weighting over registry entries is deterministic.
data.validation_requirement: Any weighted blend must beat equal weight and the best single model on held-out data before it is called consensus — the standing NFL ensemble rule.
data.risks_limitations: Error-correlation estimates need seasons of graded receipts; until then only descriptive summaries ship.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.
Implemented the deterministic Elo baseline and fixed-parameter backtest.
Published ratings, calibration bins, market comparison and generated model card.

data.delivery_note: The baseline is live and reproducible, but retrodictive and ungraded; no prospective 2026 claim is made.
data.name: Continuous Elo / Glicko Rating
data.rationale: An independently reproducible continuous rating updated after games — an interpretable challenger and baseline, not presumed to outperform other systems.
data.expected_value: The permanent simple benchmark, playing the role 538 Classic Elo plays on the NFL side.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical games only.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — pure recurrence over results.
data.validation_requirement: Reproducible from published parameters; graded through receipts like every other registry system.
data.risks_limitations: Deliberately simple: no talent, injury or market information.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Opponent-Adjusted Unit Ratings
data.rationale: Ratings at the unit level — pass offense, pass defense, rush offense, rush defense, special teams, pressure, pass protection — instead of relying solely on team-level power ratings, translated where appropriate into game-level forecasts.
data.expected_value: The structure the matchup engine reads; team-level ratings conceal exactly the edges this exposes.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays and the team-week layer with opponent adjustment.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — published unit ratings are deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Unit ratings must demonstrate incremental game-forecast value over team-level ratings before the translation is trusted.
data.risks_limitations: Unit-level samples are small; opponent adjustment errors compound at this granularity.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Data Dawgs Predictive Power Rating
data.rationale: The house predictive model — developed only after canonical data, receipts and baseline infrastructure exist, and promoted only on demonstrated incremental out-of-sample value over simpler alternatives.
data.expected_value: A Data Dawgs rating in the registry graded on the same receipts as everyone else.
data.data_source_requirements: The team-week layer, talent features, the market benchmark and a working receipts pipeline.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — published ratings and projections are deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Out-of-sample receipts against market, SP+, Elo and simple EPA regression baselines; a model card before promotion.
data.risks_limitations: The largest overfitting surface on this roadmap; deliberately sequenced near the end for that reason.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Deep / trajectory model
components.summary: Forecast future team state/feature vectors and simulate games rather than estimating static team strength. Not promoted because it uses neural networks; it must beat reasonable baselines out-of-sample.

components.name: XGBoost / other ML challengers
components.summary: Gradient-boosted and similar challengers as potential ensemble components, benchmarked against market, SP+, Elo, simple EPA regression and other simple interpretable models.

data.notes: Consolidation: the deep/trajectory and XGBoost headings become one challenger laboratory; each hypothesis is preserved as a named component with its own benchmark requirement.
data.name: Challenger Model Laboratory
data.rationale: One laboratory for experimental challenger models with two distinct hypotheses: trajectory simulation of future team state, and ML challengers over engineered features. Complexity earns no special treatment in either.
data.expected_value: Occasional genuine challengers and ensemble components; cheap, well-bounded failures otherwise.
data.data_source_requirements: The team-week layer, talent features and graded receipts for honest benchmarking.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Only for models that survive the lab and publish frozen outputs.
data.validation_requirement: Every challenger is graded through receipts against the standing baselines; failing challengers go to the Graveyard with a postmortem.
data.risks_limitations: Experimental models are explicitly allowed to fail; the risk is letting one ship before it has beaten a baseline.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: CFBD Model Training Pack / Educational Resources
source_headings: CFBD Model Training Pack / educational modeling resources
data.rationale: Potential reference or educational resource. Do not create a dependency on paid training material if open tooling already provides the required capability.
data.expected_value: Methodological reference while building house models.
data.data_source_requirements: None beyond the material itself.
data.validation_requirement: A concrete capability gap that open tooling does not already cover.
data.risks_limitations: Paid-material dependency for capability that may be free elsewhere.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Portal flow network
components.summary: Transfers as a directed talent-flow network: net importers/exporters, where talent flows, feeder programs, who attracts high-value portal talent, ecosystem centralization, and how portal acquisition relates to subsequent performance — with graph statistics and null-model comparisons.

components.name: Portal net flow
components.summary: The scalar view of the same ledger: talent gained versus lost per program, eventually integrated with team strength and counterfactual tools.

data.notes: Consolidation: Transfer Portal Flow Network and Portal Net Flow merge into one canonical entry; both underlying concepts are preserved as components.
data.name: Transfer Portal Flow Network & Net Flow
data.rationale: The flow network and net-flow metric are two views of one portal ledger: the graph explains structure, the net-flow number feeds team-strength and counterfactual work.
data.expected_value: Structural answers about the portal ecosystem plus a per-program net talent signal.
data.data_source_requirements: Portal entries and destinations keyed to canonical rosters and talent ratings.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — network statistics and net-flow are deterministic over the ledger.
data.validation_requirement: Null-model comparisons for network claims; net-flow must demonstrate incremental value before entering any forecast.
data.risks_limitations: Portal timing and rating coverage are uneven; per-player value weights are modelled, not observed.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Recruiting acquisition network
components.summary: School ↔ geography/hometown/state recruiting networks: structural footprints, pipelines and their changes through time.

components.name: Unified player acquisition graph
components.summary: High-school recruiting and portal acquisition unified into one talent-acquisition view. caleb-chandler/cfb-player-acquisition-network is a methodological reference if still appropriate, not a hard production dependency.

data.notes: Consolidation: Recruiting Acquisition Network and Player Acquisition Graph merge; the geography network and the unified graph are preserved as components.
data.name: Player Acquisition Network
data.rationale: The recruiting-geography network and the unified acquisition graph are one capability at two zoom levels; building them separately would duplicate the identity and graph plumbing.
data.expected_value: Where programs source talent, how pipelines shift, and one graph covering both acquisition channels.
data.data_source_requirements: Recruiting classes with geography plus portal moves, keyed to canonical rosters.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — graph queries over a dated snapshot.
data.validation_requirement: Descriptive structure first; any predictive claim needs the incremental-information test.
data.risks_limitations: Hometown/geography data quality varies; graph aesthetics can outrun analytical content.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Returning Production
data.rationale: Returning production is a first-class preseason and early-season signal, not a footnote inside someone else’s rating.
data.expected_value: A dated returning-production feature per team feeding preseason priors and early-season adjustments.
data.data_source_requirements: CFBD returning production reconciled against canonical rosters and portal moves.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — published feature values are deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Demonstrated early-season predictive value versus priors without it.
data.risks_limitations: Definition sensitivity: portal-era roster churn changes what "returning" means year to year.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Recruiting / Talent Composite
data.rationale: Maintain talent acquisition as an independent feature family instead of burying it inside a single rating.
data.expected_value: Composite talent features that models can include or exclude explicitly, keeping talent and performance signals separable.
data.data_source_requirements: CFBD recruiting and talent composites, dated per season.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — feature reads.
data.validation_requirement: Incremental value versus performance-only features before entering any forecast.
data.risks_limitations: Composites embed upstream rating choices Data Dawgs does not control.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

A demonstrated question CFBD data cannot answer

data.rationale: Possible incremental information exists, but CFBD already provides cleaned recruiting data. Scraping adds fragility, legal/ToS questions and permanent maintenance for undemonstrated gain.
data.expected_value: Marginal recruiting detail beyond the cleaned composites — currently unproven.
data.data_source_requirements: Would require scraping vendor sites against their terms of service.
data.validation_requirement: A demonstrated incremental need that CFBD data cannot satisfy, plus a lawful ingestion route.
data.risks_limitations: Fragile scrapers, ToS exposure and ongoing maintenance — the exact source-risk profile the NFL side declines.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

A credible dataset with known coverage appears
New evidence that even coarse NIL signals carry predictive lift
data.name: NIL Deal Tracking / Valuation
data.rationale: Sparse observations, opaque private deals, inconsistent definitions and self-reported numbers make any precise "NIL value" metric false precision today. The hypothesis stays alive; the metric does not ship.
data.expected_value: If defensible data ever exists: a market-structure signal for talent acquisition.
data.data_source_requirements: Currently unavailable at defensible quality; would need consistent, verifiable deal data.
data.validation_requirement: Coverage and definition audits before any number is published.
data.risks_limitations: Every input class is unreliable: private, self-reported, inconsistently defined.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Decision engine
components.summary: Deterministic game-state answers — "4th-and-3 at the opponent 41, up four with 8:13 remaining: go, punt or kick?" — returning the expected result of each choice and the decision advantage, not prose-only advice. Built on the open CFB fourth-down / EPA / WP modeling ecosystem.

components.name: Yards-gained distribution model
components.summary: Supporting model: the existing SportsDataverse multi-class yards-distribution methodology, evaluated for whether it should feed the conversion outcomes inside the engine.

data.notes: Consolidation: the yards-gained distribution model is preserved as a supporting component of the decision engine rather than a separate card.
data.name: Fourth-Down Decision Engine
data.rationale: One of the best architectural fits for Data Dawgs: a bounded deterministic calculation an AI can call and a human can check.
data.expected_value: Per-choice expected value and decision advantage for any fourth-down state; the substrate for coaching scorecards.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays with EPA/WP; the open fourth-down modeling ecosystem as scientific substrate.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — the defining example on this roadmap.
data.validation_requirement: Calibration of the underlying WP/EPA models on held-out CFB seasons; decision outputs benchmarked against the open ecosystem’s published results.
data.risks_limitations: CFB clock rules, pace and talent gaps differ from the NFL; imported assumptions must be re-validated, not assumed.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: CPOE Layer
data.rationale: Completion probability over expectation as a player/team analytical layer where useful — a known-good construct ported to CFB data.
data.expected_value: QB and team passing evaluation less polluted by depth-of-target and situation mix.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays with the fields a completion-probability model needs.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — published CPOE aggregates are deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: The completion-probability model gets a model card; CPOE stays descriptive until incremental predictive value is shown.
data.risks_limitations: CFB pass-level data quality varies more than NFL; expected-completion calibration must be checked per season.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: xREPA (Expected Rushing EPA)
data.rationale: Expected rushing EPA as an analytical and player-evaluation capability — with a clearly documented model card and definition required from the start.
data.expected_value: Rushing evaluation that separates situation from execution.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays with rushing context fields.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — published aggregates are deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: A documented model card and definition before any number is published; descriptive until incremental value is shown.
data.risks_limitations: Definition drift is the known failure mode for expected-rushing constructs; hence the model-card requirement in the source roadmap.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Matchup Fingerprints
data.rationale: Overall ratings conceal matchup-specific structure. Represent strengths and weaknesses across pass offense × pass defense, rush offense × rush defense, pressure × pass protection, explosiveness × explosive prevention, early downs × early downs, red zone × red zone, and havoc × ball security.
data.expected_value: Named, quantified matchup edges for any pairing — the analytical answer to "where is this game actually won".
data.data_source_requirements: Opponent-adjusted unit ratings across the fingerprint dimensions.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — edge-finding over published unit ratings is deterministic.
data.validation_requirement: Edges must demonstrate forecast value beyond team-level ratings before being presented as predictive rather than descriptive.
data.risks_limitations: Depends entirely on unit-rating quality; noisy units produce confident-looking false edges.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Counterfactual Simulator
data.rationale: Controlled what-if scenarios: different returning production, altered portal additions/losses, injuries/availability where reliable, different game outcomes, different team-strength assumptions — with uncertainty explicit.
data.expected_value: Disciplined counterfactuals instead of vibes: what actually changes if an assumption changes.
data.data_source_requirements: The ratings registry plus the talent/portal feature families being perturbed.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — declared perturbation in, distribution out, reproducibly.
data.validation_requirement: Every scenario labelled simulation; uncertainty bands mandatory; no counterfactual presented as observation.
data.risks_limitations: Counterfactuals inherit every modelling assumption underneath them; false precision is the standing hazard.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.
Implemented an exact caller-supplied hypothetical schedule-path distribution over the dated Elo registry; actual schedules, standings, tiebreakers and playoff selection remain unbuilt.

data.delivery_note: Partially implemented as staged dd_project_cfb_schedule_path: exact Poisson-binomial win-count distributions for up to 20 caller-supplied matchups using fixed end-of-2025 Elo. It is not an actual 2026 schedule, conference simulation or playoff model and remains non-callable in production.

components.name: Season Monte Carlo
components.summary: Monte Carlo the remainder of a season: expected record, conference championship probability, playoff probability, seed distribution and conditional paths — "what happens to Ohio State’s playoff path if they lose to Oregon?"

components.name: Game leverage index
components.summary: Derived capability of the same simulator: which remaining games swing conference/playoff outcomes most, computed by differencing conditional simulations.

data.notes: Consolidation: Game Leverage Index is preserved as a derived component of the simulator rather than a separate card.
data.name: Schedule Path Simulator
data.rationale: The leverage index is a derived output of the path simulator, not a second engine; one simulation core serves both.
data.expected_value: Playoff odds, seed distributions, conditional paths and per-game leverage from a single reproducible simulator.
data.data_source_requirements: The ratings registry for game probabilities plus canonical schedules and tiebreak/selection rules.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — seeded simulation with declared inputs is reproducible.
data.validation_requirement: Simulated probabilities carry their input ratings and date; selection-committee modelling is labelled as modelled, not rule-derived.
data.risks_limitations: Playoff selection is a committee, not a formula; that model layer carries irreducible uncertainty.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Prediction-Market Integration
data.rationale: Prediction-market prices as another independent consensus signal — when sufficiently liquid and reliable CFB contracts exist. Market probability is a signal, not truth.
data.expected_value: An additional independent belief in the registry, useful precisely because its errors correlate differently.
data.data_source_requirements: Liquid CFB contracts with dated, attributable prices.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — dated price reads.
data.validation_requirement: Liquidity thresholds declared before inclusion; thin markets excluded rather than smoothed.
data.risks_limitations: CFB prediction-market liquidity is currently thin and uneven across games.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.
Published a results-only record-versus-scoring divergence baseline with one-score records; no predictive labels are permitted yet.
A leakage-resistant chronological holdout found a small incremental signal beyond Elo; the one-season retrodictive result keeps the detector evaluating and does not permit team labels.

data.delivery_note: The descriptive baseline now has a one-season, pregame-only chronological holdout: one Elo-offset coefficient improved Brier by 0.001123 and log loss by 0.002277 over 233 untouched games. A staged read-only MCP explorer exposes the dated gaps and aggregate receipt without labels. This remains retrodictive, not market-adjusted or prospective, and does not authorize overrated/underrated team labels.
data.name: Overrated / Underrated Team Detector
data.rationale: Identify gaps between observed results and underlying performance from record, point differential, EPA, success rate, postgame win expectancy, turnover variance, fourth-down variance, opponent strength, close-game results and market/SP+/FPI/Data Dawgs ratings. The calculation quantifies divergence; "fraud" is a brand, not a method.
data.expected_value: Expected record, luck index, underlying performance rank, market over/undervaluation and uncertainty — one of the strongest potential weekly CFB products.
data.data_source_requirements: The team-week layer, ratings registry and market dataset.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — declared divergence formulas over published inputs.
data.validation_requirement: Divergence must demonstrate forward predictive value (does "fraud" regress?) before any claim beyond description; outputs carry uncertainty.
data.risks_limitations: Luck metrics are seductive and noisy at CFB sample sizes; the label must never outrun the calculation.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Coaching trees
components.summary: Coaching movement, ancestry, coordinator relationships, scheme inheritance and tenure as structural data. Interesting; predictive/decision value must be demonstrated.

components.name: Movement / performance delta
components.summary: Performance changes associated with coaching and coordinator transitions, controlling for obvious confounders (talent, schedule, roster churn).

data.notes: Consolidation: Coaching Trees and Coaching Movement / Performance Delta merge into one lab; both hypotheses are preserved as components.
data.name: Coaching Networks & Transition Effects Lab
data.rationale: The tree is the structure and the performance delta is the test of whether that structure predicts anything; one lab covers both, sharing the same coaching-history dataset.
data.expected_value: If the delta analysis shows signal, a coaching-transition feature; if not, a documented negative result.
data.data_source_requirements: A coaching/coordinator history dataset keyed to canonical teams and seasons — itself a build.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Only if promoted: tree queries and transition features would be deterministic reads.
data.validation_requirement: Transition effects must survive confounder controls and the incremental-information test before entering any forecast.
data.risks_limitations: Coaching changes correlate with everything else changing at once; attribution is genuinely hard.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: Coaching Decision Scorecards
data.rationale: Separate coaching decision quality from realized outcomes across fourth-down decisions, timeout usage, two-point decisions, clock management, aggression and decision EPA/WP. Do not punish a mathematically correct decision because it happened to fail.
data.expected_value: Season-long decision-quality grading per staff — philosophically the most Data Dawgs product on this roadmap.
data.data_source_requirements: Canonical plays plus the fourth-down engine’s per-choice expected values.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — scorecards are deterministic aggregation over graded decisions.
data.validation_requirement: The underlying decision models must be calibrated first; scorecards inherit and must disclose their assumptions.
data.risks_limitations: Decision EPA/WP models embed assumptions coaches may rationally reject (roster, injury, weather context the model cannot see).

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Weather effects
components.summary: Test whether detailed weather features provide stable incremental forecast value.

components.name: Altitude
components.summary: Test the effect instead of assuming its magnitude.

components.name: Travel distance / time zones
components.summary: Test incremental value after controlling for team strength and venue.

components.name: Indoor / outdoor effects
components.summary: Potential interaction with weather and team style.

data.notes: Consolidation: Weather, Altitude, Travel/Time Zones and Indoor/Outdoor merge into one contextual-effects lab; each hypothesis is preserved as a separately testable component.
data.name: Contextual Effects Lab (Weather / Altitude / Travel / Venue)
data.rationale: Four environmental hypotheses sharing one experimental design: engineer the feature, control for team strength and venue, and run the same incremental-information test. A single lab prevents four copies of the same harness.
data.expected_value: Whichever contextual features genuinely survive testing enter forecasts; the rest become documented negative results.
data.data_source_requirements: Venue metadata, historical weather, travel/time-zone derivations joined to canonical games.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Only for features that graduate.
data.validation_requirement: Each component is separately tested against the no-context baseline; stable out-of-sample lift required for promotion.
data.risks_limitations: Contextual effects are small, collinear and easy to overfit; that is exactly why they are lab work.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

components.name: Structured injury / availability data
components.summary: Potentially valuable, but data quality and reliable historical snapshots are major concerns. Explore trustworthy structured sources before relying on anything scraped.

components.name: Practice participation / beat-writer proxies
components.summary: Potential signal, but unstructured-data maintenance and historical reproducibility could be expensive. Higher source risk than structured feeds — evidence of incremental value required before productionization.

data.notes: Consolidation: the two availability headings merge into one lab while their differing source-risk recommendations are preserved per component (structured: lab; beat-writer proxies: defer).
data.name: Injury & Availability Signals Lab
data.rationale: Availability is one signal family with two source classes carrying different risk: structured feeds are worth exploring now; beat-writer proxies are deferred until the structured route is exhausted and value is demonstrated.
data.expected_value: If historical snapshots prove reliable: one of the few context signals with plausible material forecast value.
data.data_source_requirements: Structured availability sources with reproducible historical snapshots; snapshots frozen at forecast time, like receipts.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Only for signals that graduate.
data.validation_requirement: Historical reproducibility audit first — an availability signal that cannot be reconstructed as-of game time cannot be validated at all.
data.risks_limitations: CFB injury reporting is inconsistent by conference and era; retroactive data quietly leaks outcomes.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

Evidence emerges that sentiment leads rather than follows results
A specific bounded question (e.g. coaching pressure) shows measurable lift
data.name: Media / Reddit / Social Sentiment
data.rationale: A potential experimental signal for coaching pressure or recruiting momentum, but likely noisy, endogenous, hard to reproduce, expensive to maintain and prone to narrative contamination.
data.expected_value: Speculative; retained as an idea, not a current priority.
data.data_source_requirements: Social/media firehoses with archival for reproducibility — expensive before any value is shown.
data.validation_requirement: Reproducible historical corpus plus demonstrated lift over public information already in the registry.
data.risks_limitations: Sentiment often just restates record and market — endogeneity is the default outcome.

lifecycle_history.note: Entered The Pound from the 2026-08-08 CFB roadmap.

data.name: ESPN Total QBR Historical Layer
data.rationale: Investigate the incremental analytical value and a permitted, reliable ingestion route. Do not duplicate existing open functionality unnecessarily.
data.expected_value: A QB evaluation layer to test against CPOE/xREPA — kept only if it adds information.
data.data_source_requirements: A permitted, reliable QBR ingestion route with dated snapshots.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Only if adopted: historical reads.
data.validation_requirement: Incremental value over the in-house passing layers before any dependency is created.
data.risks_limitations: Proprietary metric with an opaque method; ingestion permission and stability are unverified.

lifecycle_history.note: Captured as the read-only deterministic interface for validated CFB capabilities.

Implemented and evaluated team profile, comparison, hypothetical Elo matchup, exact hypothetical schedule-path, descriptive record-divergence and blocked model-disagreement evidence tools locally; all remain staged and non-callable in production.

data.delivery_note: Six source-backed CFB tools are implemented locally and staged, including exact matchup and schedule-path calculations plus no-label divergence and blocked-study evidence readers. Production still has 26 live tools; deployment requires a separate approved Worker release.
data.name: Deterministic CFB MCP/API Tool Layer
data.rationale: The eventual product layer: read-only tools that call deterministic Data Dawgs computation, with the AI doing orchestration and explanation — the same architecture as the 26 live NFL-side tools, extended to CFB only as each underlying capability ships.
data.expected_value: AI-callable CFB answers backed by receipts instead of vibes.
data.data_source_requirements: Each candidate tool depends on its underlying capability existing and being validated first.
data.deterministic_tool_potential: Yes — this entry is the tool layer itself.
data.validation_requirement: A candidate tool goes live only after its underlying computation is built, tested and deployed — the same gate the NFL calculators passed. None of these names is callable today.
data.risks_limitations: The temptation is registering tool names before the computation earns them; the Pound exists to prevent exactly that.

The existing language layer becomes unavailable

data.rationale: A separate Ollama/report-writing architecture duplicates the language layer Claude/GPT/Toto already provide. A deterministic analytical capability is more valuable than another generated summary.
data.expected_value: None over the existing architecture.
data.data_source_requirements: None.
data.validation_requirement: Not applicable while redundant.
